newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea warns of trade danger from strikes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea warns of trade danger from strikes.

text.p: South Korean Trade Minister Ahn Kwang-koo warned on Wednesday the current wave of strikes could make it harder for the country to control its snowballing trade deficit this year than last year.
The deficit totalled an estimated $20 billion in 1996. Fears that the deficit could spin further out of control sent the Korean won plunging to a new six-year low on Wednesday.
The country's 1995 trade deficit totalled $10.06 billion.

Ahn told a meeting of economic and security-related ministers that strikes disrupting industry must end quickly. "Trade Minister Ahn Kwang-koo reported to the meeting that unless the strikes end soon, controlling the trade account would be seriously worse this year than last year," a government statement said.

The won opened at 849.00 against the dollar on Wednesday, its lowest level since interbank trading began in March 1990, indicating concern over the long-term outlook for the nation's exports, dealers said.
Strikes that have swept South Korea since a controversial labour law was rammed though parliament on December 26 have cost the country $400 million in lost exports, according to the government.
